title: Runtime Entropy and Upgrade Safety Playbook for Private Deployments
author: Marco Liu
content:
Overview

This playbook defines an operator-ready, low-risk procedure for upgrading runtime components and model artifacts in private (VPC and on-prem) deployments while actively managing "runtime entropy"—the divergence between expected runtime state and live system state (config drift, KV cache inconsistencies, quantization/profile mismatches, and asymmetric node configuration). It covers preflight checks, phased rollout steps, automated and manual rollback actions, telemetry/health thresholds, and customer-facing validation required for acceptance.

Scope

- Applies to Redwood Private control plane and runtime stacks (service names: rwd-controlplane, rwd-agent, rwd-runtime, rwd-kvcache).
- Targeted upgrade types: runtime binary (minor/major), model artifact swap (weights/quantization), KV cache schema changes, and packaging (image/firmware) updates.
- Excludes hardware firmware upgrades (see hw-eol-deprecation playbook).

Goals

- Maintain 99.5% request success rate during upgrade windows for production tenants.
- Keep 95th percentile token latency regression within +10% of baseline for 2 hours post-rollout.
- Provide deterministic rollback within 15 minutes for single-service regressions and 60 minutes for multi-service failure modes.

Key definitions

- Runtime entropy: measurable divergence from expected runtime state (config, KV cache, model weights) that increases probability of silent failures or output regression.
- Safe window: period after rollout where metrics are observed against acceptance criteria.

Risk model and primary failure modes

1. KV cache incompatibility: new runtime expects different cache key structure leading to cold starts or wrong outputs.
2. Quantization mismatch: swapped model quantization causes degraded quality/regressions.
3. Partial rollout divergence: mixed-version traffic returns differing outputs and fails eval parity checks.
4. Control plane drift: mis-synced feature flags or routing causing tenant mis-routing.

Preconditions (hard gates before any upgrade)

- Backups and snapshots completed: control plane DB snapshot (rwd-cp-snapshot), KV cache snapshot (where supported) and model artifact registry snapshot.
- Customer acceptance test (CAT) harness uploaded to runbook: basic prompt set (10 prompts) and evaluation script (python) per-customer.
- Capacity buffer: 20% burstable capacity reserved on Dedicated pools or on-prem operator nodes flagged for maintenance.
- Communication: SRE/SE oncall and customer POC notified at least 24 hours prior for >minor upgrades.

Preflight checklist (automated plus manual)

1. Sanity automation (CI-generated): integration smoke passing for rwd-runtime and rwd-agent images (CI tag: release/<tag>).
2. Canary lab: run synthetic load at target QPS for 30m against a canary cluster.
3. KV schema validation: run `rwd-kvctl validate-schema --target release/<tag>` to assert compatibility.
4. Model checksum/parity: `sha256sum model-v<new>.tar.gz` must match checksum in artifact registry.
5. Eval parity: run customer CAT harness and compare embedding/cosine similarity and token-level divergence metrics.

Phased rollout steps (recommended)

Phase 0 — Staging verification (operator):
- Deploy release to staging control plane and runtime.
- Run automated acceptance: unit tests, integration tests, and full CAT harness.
- Confirm monitoring dashboards (rwd-dashboard/staging) show baseline SLOs.

Phase 1 — Small canary (1–3 nodes / 1–5% traffic):
- Route a small percentage of traffic using canary policy `routing.canary=on`.
- Observe live evals (see Telemetry) for at least 45 minutes.
- Run `rwd-ops check-health --tenants sample_tenant_list.txt` and ensure no tenant reports >2% request errors.

Phase 2 — Regional ramp (25% traffic or 2 AZs):
- Increase traffic to 25% in a single region or two availability zones (AZs).
- Run CVR/QA evals: automated reranker and completion-quality tests.
- Observe latency P95 and P99. Abort if thresholds breached.

Phase 3 — Global/All tenants (100%):
- After green light from Phase 2, ramp to 100% using rolling update.
- Keep burst capacity for 60 minutes and SRE on-call paging active.

Monitoring and telemetry (what to watch)

Primary metrics and thresholds (abort if any triggered):
- Request success rate (per-tenant): target >= 99.5%. Abort if any tenant drops below 98.0% for 10 consecutive minutes.
- Token-level latency: P95 change <= +10% and P99 change <= +25% relative to baseline. Abort if exceeded for 15m window.
- Model quality regressions: median embedding cosine similarity to baseline lower by >0.03 on CAT harness. Abort.
- Error class spikes: decoder OOM, kernel-failure counts > 5/min system-wide. Abort and roll back.

Telemetry sampling guidance (cost-aware):
- Default sampling: 10% full trace + 1% full request payload capture across production tenants.
- For canaries: 100% full trace + 100% payload capture for canary tenant IDs.
- Adaptive sampling: increase to 20% full trace if P95 latency deviates >5%.
- Retention: full samples retained for 7 days; aggregated metrics retained per standard retention policy.

Automated validation hooks (examples)

- Health probe: `curl -fsS http://<node>/healthz` must return 200 and JSON {"status":"ok","kv_synced":true}.
- KV-check: `rwd-kvctl compare --baseline /snapshots/kv_preupgrade --live` returns zero mismatches.
- Model inference parity: run `python scripts/compare_inference.py --old model-vX --new model-vY --prompts cat_prompts.json` and assert token-diff <= 1.2% and embedding-sim >= 0.96.

Abort criteria and automated rollback triggers

- Immediate rollback triggers (automated):
  - kernel-failure rate > 0.5% of requests for 5 minutes.
  - Unexpected KV mismatch count > 50 per minute.
  - Cat harness quality metric breach (see thresholds above).

- Manual abort triggers:
  - Customer POC reports reproducible functional regression.
  - Sustained latency or error trend with no clear mitigation within 30 minutes.

Rollback procedure (fast path for common failures)

1. Freeze rollouts: set `routing.upgrade_pause = true` in control plane flags.
2. Switch traffic back: update routing policy and GradualShift rollback to previous release tag: `rwd-ctl traffic-shift --from release/<new> --to release/<old> --pace 100% --force` (fast path: immediate).
3. Rehydrate KV: if KV incompatibility detected, restore snapshot: `rwd-kvctl restore --snapshot /snapshots/kv_preupgrade --force` and then run `rwd-kvctl warm-cache --target all`.
4. Confirm model artifact swap-back: re-push prior model artifact `rwd-artifact push --file model-v<old>.tar.gz --set-active`.
5. Run sanity checks: `rwd-ops check-health --all` and verify SLOs.
6. Post-rollback communication: immediately notify customers with the templated message below and create an incident in incidenttracker (INC- auto-generated).

Rollback verification checklist

- Control plane health: all components show status "ok".
- KV consistency: zero critical mismatches.
- Model parity: CAT harness within thresholds.
- Latency: P95 returned to baseline within 30 minutes.

Operational runbook scripts and snippets

- Snapshot control plane DB
  - `kubectl exec -n rwd-system rwd-cp-0 -- rwd-cp-tool snapshot create --output /tmp/cp-snap-$(date +%s).tar.gz`
- Warm KV cache (operator helper)
  - `rwd-kvctl warm-cache --tenant-id TENANT_ID --prefetch 1000`
- Quick rollback (one liner)
  - `rwd-ctl rollback --target release/<old> --scope region:us-east-1 --force`

Customer acceptance and fields validation

- Provide customer POC with an acceptance checklist and run CAT harness during Phase 2.
- Required customer signoff items: 1) functional smoke tests pass, 2) latency within acceptance, 3) no dataflow regressions reported.
- Example acceptance email template (send on green):
  - Subject: "[Redwood] Private deployment upgrade complete — validation request"
  - Body: "We completed the staged rollout to your environment. Please run the attached CAT harness (link) and report any anomalies within 48 hours. Contact SE oncall: se-oncall@redwood.ai"

Escalation and ownership

- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments SRE team (oncall alias: rwd-sre-oncall).
- Secondary owner: runtime platform (runtime@redwood.ai).
- SLA/NFR escalation: if rollback exceeds 60 minutes or customer impact affects revenue-bound SLAs, escalate to Director of SRE and Customer Success immediately.

Post-upgrade audit and continuous improvement

- Create a short post-upgrade report within 24 hours: include metrics, anomalies, corrective actions, and retro notes.
- Required fields in report: change-id, release tags, pre/post SLO metrics, canary tenant IDs, CAT harness results.
- If rollback occurred, capture root cause analysis within 72 hours and attach for compliance evidence.

Appendix A — Templates and quick checks

- `rwd-ops check-health` expected output snippet:
  - {"status":"ok", "uptime":3600, "kv_synced":true, "active_release":"release/<tag>"}
- Minimal CAT harness example (python):
  - `python -c "from rwd_eval import Runner; Runner('model-vX').run('prompts.json')"`
